Selected article: Gorbatenko K M and Melnikov I V (2019). Trophodynamics of marine organisms in the epipelagic layer of the Okhotsk Sea in the 2000s. Izvestiya TINRO 198, 143–163.
Other known articles: Chaikina (2004), A trophic mass-balance model of the Sea of Okhotsk for the 1980s period. Original thesis unavailable; related 2020 chapter retained.
Radchenko (2015), Characterization of the Sea of Okhotsk Ecosystem Based on Ecosystem Modelling. A 48-group contemporary alternative is retained.
Selected model: 52_GM2019_Fig9_Pelagic_balanced_(2000-2014). Whole-Sea epipelagic reconstruction of Figure 9 and source feeding tables; 2000–2014. Twenty two source groups, including detritus, plus a synthetic external-food import.
Other models from the same article: Figure 9 is the generalized pelagic energy-flow network for the 2000s. Figure 10 summarizes production by its components. Figure-only and text-plus-Figure calculations are reconstruction variants; the dissertation's shelf-bottom network is a separate supporting-source model.
Selection rationale: Article - The requested reconstruction uses the accessible whole-Sea production and feeding synthesis for 2000–2014, a more recent period than the previous 1980s model.

Model - The source-carbon Figure 9 network retains microbes and detritus and can be completed with the source feeding tables. The adopted variant follows the requested preference for plausible balance with minimal departures.
Geographic fit: A. Region covered by study: approximately 100% under the intended whole-Sea domain approximation.
B. Study covered by region: approximately 100% under that approximation.
Temporal fit: The source network represents 2000–2014; the jellyfish feeding tables represent 2006–2014. The catch series spans 1950–2019 and the coverage reference is 2019. Fixed coefficients and biomass-based allocation extend average source-era relationships to earlier and later catches without resolving annual ecosystem or catch-composition change.
